title: lpw-world
label: Jake MacKenna

won.source: The promotion's own Clash of the Champions card, 13 April 2002, Ice Palace, Tampa.

lost.source: Called the reigning LPW champion on 19 April 2002 and the former champion on 3 May; how and when he lost the belt is not in the record.

how: Pinned Kobra Khan under Superfight rules for the vacant title after Devastator chokeslammed Khan, hit him with the Annihilator and threw MacKenna on top of him.

title: lpw-world
label: Andrew Dixon

won.source: Billed as the LPW champion on 3 May 2002; Jake MacKenna was still champion on 19 April, and the card on which Dixon won the belt is not in the record.

lost.source: The promotion's own Special Report of 5 May 2002.

how: Won on a card that is not in the record, between 19 April and 3 May 2002.
note: Called out by Dead Skull on 3 May 2002, when a masked figure accepted Dixon's Doomsday challenge to Devastator; vacated the belt on 5 May.

title: lpw-tag-team
label: the Shadowlords

won.source: The promotion's own Tuesday Night Clash, 12 March 2002, Mobile Civic Center.

how: Beat Zula Bon Bimbay and Rock And Roll Rebel for the vacant title with the Arctic Inferno after a fireball blinded Rebel.
note: Retained against Terminator and Shi'Noku on 15 March 2002.

title: lpw-tag-team
label: the Oriental Assassins

won.source: The promotion's own Tuesday Night Clash, 9 April 2002.

how: Pinned Ice after darts from an unseen figure felled both Shadowlords.
note: Left the promotion after losing the belts.

title: lpw-tag-team
label: the Puerto Rican Slayers

won.source: The promotion's own Clash of the Champions card, 13 April 2002.

how: Won the Final Confrontation superfight against the Oriental Assassins, Suicidal ending it with the Assisted Suicide.
note: Retained against kYd-X and Bull Dozer on 19 April 2002 (Dead Skull and Suicidal defending) and kept the belts through a disqualification loss on 3 May (Songi and Suicidal defending).

title: lpw-lightweight
label: Rock And Roll Rebel

won.source: Billed as the champion on 9 April 2002; the 19 March announcement set a five-man tournament to start on 22 March, and the cards that decided it are not in the record.

lost.source: Dead Skull carried the Lightweight belt on 3 May 2002; how it changed hands is not in the record.

how: Champion by 9 April 2002; a five-man tournament for the vacant title began on 22 March, and the cards that decided it are not in the record.
note: Kept the belt against Dragon Ninja on 9 April 2002.

title: lpw-lightweight
label: Dead Skull

won.source: Carried the Lightweight belt on 3 May 2002; the card on which he won it is not in the record.

how: Won on a card that is not in the record, between 9 April and 3 May 2002.

title: lpw-national
label: Wesley Potter

won.source: The promotion's own Clash of the Champions card, 13 April 2002.

how: Pinned Johnny Ziro for the vacant title with the Final Cut pedigree after a masked Assassin interfered.
note: Billed as the United States National champion; forfeited a non-title match on 3 May 2002.

title: lpw-superfight
label: Kobra Khan

won.source: The promotion's own Friday Frenzy, 15 March 2002, Georgia Dome.

lost.source: Dead Skull carried the Superfight belt on 3 May 2002; how it changed hands is not in the record.

how: Won a career-ending steel cage match against Hurricane Wild Child for the vacant title.
note: Retained against Devastator on 19 April 2002 after Andrew Dixon and Paul Setzer shocked Devastator with a defibrillator.

title: lpw-superfight
label: Dead Skull

won.source: Carried the Superfight belt on 3 May 2002; the card on which he won it is not in the record.

how: Won on a card that is not in the record, between 19 April and 3 May 2002.
note: A masked figure took the belt from his shoulder on 3 May and promised to come back for it after Doomsday.

title: lpw-universal
label: Zodiac

won.source: The promotion's own Friday Frenzy, 3 May 2002, Madison Square Garden.

how: Beat Adam Simon two falls to one in a best-of-three-falls superfight, ending it with the Big Bang on the commentary table.

title: lpw-universal
label: Adam Simon

won.source: Billed as the Undisputed Universal champion on 3 May 2002; where and when he won the belt is not in the record.

how: Held before 3 May 2002; the record does not say how he won it.
